faq.flyQ: Can I fly “{name}” without installing anything?
faq.flyA: Yes. Open the scene in a desktop browser with WebGPU (Chrome or Edge), connect an EdgeTX radio over USB or a gamepad, or use the keyboard, and fly. It is free and nothing is installed.
faq.wallsQ: Does the drone crash into the walls of “{name}”?
faq.wallsYesA: Yes. The scan has collision voxels{cm}, and the simulator tests the drone's whole path against them, so it crashes, tumbles and respawns instead of flying through. The walls can be switched off with the C key.
faq.wallsNoA: Not yet: this scan has no collision file on SuperSplat, so the drone flies through everything. The simulator shows a "no walls" badge on such scenes.
faq.whoQ: Who made this scan, and may I use it?
faq.whoLicenseA: {author} scanned it and published it on SuperSplat under {license}. The simulator loads it from SuperSplat's CDN and credits the author on screen; for any other use, follow the licence.
faq.whoNoLicenseA: {author} scanned it and published it on SuperSplat without a stated licence. The simulator only loads it from SuperSplat's CDN and credits the author; ask the author before using it anywhere else.
faq.sizeA: About {mb} MB. It streams from SuperSplat's CDN, coarse detail first, so you can fly before it has fully loaded.
faq.windQ: Is there wind in this scene?
faq.scaleQ: Can I change the size of the scene?
faq.scaleA: Yes. The [ and ] keys scale the whole scan around the drone from ×0.25 to ×100, the walls with it: a room can fly like a city, a street like a table-top model.
